title: A centre-tap full-wave rectifier
body: A student builds a full-wave rectifier using a centre-tap transformer and two identical silicon diodes D1 and D2. The p-side of D1 is joined to end A of the transformer secondary and the p-side of D2 to end B. The n-sides of the two diodes are joined together, and a load resistor RL is connected between this common point and the centre tap of the secondary. The ac input to the primary has a frequency of 50 Hz. Because A and B are at opposite ends of the secondary, whenever A is positive with respect to the centre tap, B is negative with respect to it, and the other way round. The student observes the voltage across RL on an oscilloscope and sees pulses shaped like half sinusoids.
